title: Mouse Without Borders : 双机器多屏环境的无界鼠标使用问题
author: sGulugulu

status.label: Matches the existing external-monitor handoff bug
status.detail: The two-machine 2x2 layout in this report matches the older open Mouse Without Borders bug where cross-machine handoff works on one row but not the other when only the centerline monitors are considered.

next_action.label: Link the duplicate external-monitor handoff issue
next_action.reason: The older open issue already captures the same topology limitation and even documents the same centerline workaround pattern.

judgment.rationale: The issue describes the same cross-machine multi-monitor limitation already tracked by open issue #37159: movement works across one pair of monitors but fails across the other pair in a two-machine layout, depending on which monitors touch the centerline.
evidence: The reporter shows a two-machine 2x2 arrangement where the lower pair hand off correctly and the upper pair do not.
Open issue #37159 reports that Mouse Without Borders cannot move directly between the two external monitors in a relative multi-monitor layout.
A public workaround comment on #37159 explains that only the monitors touching the centerline participate in cross-machine handoff, which matches the row-specific failure pattern here.
Current Mouse Without Borders code still routes machine transitions through matrix and shared screen coordinate logic rather than per-monitor adjacency objects.
judgment.recommended_action: Link this report to #37159 instead of starting a second parallel fix investigation.

fix_assessment.rationale: A second repository fix should not be designed from this report because the same external-monitor handoff limitation is already tracked by open issue #37159.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders can hand off between the lower pair of monitors in a two-machine 2x2 layout but not between the upper pair. The symptom aligns with the older open centerline-limited external-monitor handoff issue.
known_information: The reporter is on PowerToys 0.100.2 on both machines and uses Windows 10.
The diagram shows a two-machine 2x2 arrangement where A/C belong to one machine and B/D belong to the other.
Movement from C to D works, but movement from A to B does not, and movement leftward from B or D jumps back to C.
There are no comments, attachments, or assignees on the live issue.
Open issue #37159 describes the same class of failure between external monitors in a two-machine layout.
inferences: The failure is likely the same centerline-monitor adjacency limitation already documented on #37159 rather than a new unique topology bug.
The row-specific behavior suggests the cross-machine routing still privileges a single touching edge rather than arbitrary per-monitor neighbors.
issue_context.analysis: The older open issue already captures both the limitation and a workaround that matches this report. Duplicate consolidation is more valuable than a fresh design artifact for the same topology family.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the full issue body, labels, assignees, and the empty live timeline.
Compared the report to open issue #37159, whose body and workaround comment describe the same external-monitor handoff limitation in a two-machine layout.

Inspected Mouse Without Borders transition code in App/Core/Common.cs and screen-coordinate handling in App/Helper/FormHelper.cs to confirm the product still routes transitions through shared matrix and coordinate logic.

actions.label: Link duplicate external-monitor handoff issue

comment.body: Thanks for documenting the 2x2 two-machine monitor layout. This appears to match the older open Mouse Without Borders issue #37159, which reports that cross-machine handoff works only for the monitors touching the centerline and not for the external/upper monitors in a multi-monitor layout. Please consolidate this report with #37159 so the monitor-topology investigation stays in one place.
